source_text: Alioquin - inquit - quid facient qui baptizantur pro mortuis, si omnino mortui non resurgunt? Quid et baptizantur pro illis? Quid et nos periclitamur omni hora? Quotidie morior per vestram gloriam, quam habeo in Domino. Si secundum hominem pugnavi bestiis Ephesi, quid mihi prodest, si mortui non resurgunt? Manducemus et bibamus, cras enim moriemur. Si, inquit, ista spes futurae gloriae, qua Deus omnia in omnibus erit, impia infidelitate quatiatur, negeturque resurrectio mortuorum, quid facient qui baptizantur pro mortuis? Natus hinc error aliquorum est, putantium inter exordia Evangelii eum morem fuisse, quo astantes pro cadaveribus profiterentur, et aqua Baptismatis etiam defunctorum membra perfunderent; quod apparet de imperitia contigisse. Hoc enim quod ait Apostolus: Baptizantur pro mortuis, nihil aliud indicat, quam illud quod ad Romanos dixit: Consepulti illi sumus per Baptisma in mortem [n230] ; id est: Qua gratia, tali ad Baptismatis susceptionem animo accedimus, ut membra nostra mortificemus in posterum, et pro mortuis omnino degamus, si spes non est, quia post mortem vivamus? Cur autem et quotidianis, inquit, subdor periculis, in mortem iugiter incidens, quam inferunt persequentes, ut de vestris ante Deum possim profectibus gloriari, si mortui non resurgunt? Cur autem et secundum hominem pugnavi bestiis Ephesi, id est, cur sustinui bestialem seditiosorum furorem, si adhuc nutat quod mortui resurgunt? Nolite seduci; bonos mores corrumpunt colloquia mala. Ignorantiam enim Dei quidam habent; ad confusionem vobis dico [n231] . Amor, inquit, peccatorum diffidere vos suadet de futuris; putatur non esse iudicium, ut maiore peccetur audacia. Omnino, inquit, nesciunt aestimare Deum, qui inficiantur resurrectioni. Non ergo solum remunerationem, sed virtutem divinitatis negatis, unde nimium debetis erubescere. Ad confusionem vobis dico, posse inter vos tales quospiam reperiri.
pass_a_gloss: Otherwise, he says, what will they do who are baptized for the dead, if the dead altogether do not rise? Why also are they baptized for them? Why also are we endangered every hour? Daily I die through your glory, which I have in the Lord. If according to a human I fought with beasts at Ephesus, what does it profit me, if the dead do not rise? Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die. If, he says, that hope of future glory, by which God will be all in all, is shaken by impious infidelity, and a resurrection of the dead is denied, what will they do who are baptized for the dead? From here an error of some was born, thinking that among the beginnings of the Gospel that custom was, by which those standing by would profess for corpses, and would pour even the members of the defunct with the water of Baptism; which appears to have happened from unskillfulness. For this which the Apostle says: They are baptized for the dead, indicates nothing other than that which he said to the Romans: We were buried with him through Baptism into death; that is: By what grace do we approach such a mind to the taking-up of Baptism, that we may mortify our members for the future, and altogether live as for the dead, if there is not a hope, because we may live after death? But why also, he says, am I subjected to daily dangers, falling continually into death, which those persecuting inflict, that I may be able to glory from your progresses before God, if the dead do not rise? But why also according to a human did I fight with beasts at Ephesus, that is, why did I sustain the bestial fury of the seditious, if it still totters that the dead rise? Do not be seduced; evil conversations corrupt good manners. For certain people have an ignorance of God; I say it to your confusion. A love, he says, of sins persuades you to distrust about future things; it is thought there is not a judgment, that it may be sinned with greater daring. Altogether, he says, they do not know how to estimate God, who disown the resurrection. You therefore deny not only a remuneration, but a virtue of divinity, whence you ought too much to blush. I say it to your confusion, that such people can be found among you.

pass_b_english: ‘Otherwise,’ he says, ‘what will those baptized for the dead do, if the dead do not rise at all? Why are they baptized for them? Why do we also face danger every hour? I die daily, by the glory I have in you in the Lord. If, humanly speaking, I fought beasts at Ephesus, what does it profit me if the dead do not rise? Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die’ (1 Corinthians 15:29–32) (Colossians 3:5).

If, he says, impious unbelief shakes this hope of future glory, in which God will be all in all, and denies resurrection of the dead, what will those baptized for the dead do? From this arose some people’s error: they think the early Gospel period had a custom whereby bystanders made the profession on behalf of corpses and even washed the dead person’s limbs with baptismal water. This plainly arose from ignorance. The apostle’s phrase ‘baptized for the dead’ indicates nothing other than what he said to the Romans: ‘We were buried with him through baptism into death’ (Romans 6:4) (Isaiah 22:13).

That is: Why do we approach baptism in a spirit of putting our members to death thereafter and living wholly as dead, if there is no hope of living after death? Why, he says, do I submit to daily dangers, constantly encountering the death persecutors inflict, so that I may boast before God of your progress, if the dead do not rise? Why, humanly speaking, did I fight beasts at Ephesus—that is, endure the beastlike fury of rioters—if resurrection of the dead is still uncertain?

‘Do not be deceived: bad conversations corrupt good morals. Some have ignorance of God; I say this to your shame’ (1 Corinthians 15:33–34) (1 Corinthians 15:28). Love of sins, he says, persuades you to distrust future things. People suppose there is no judgment so that they may sin more boldly. Those denying resurrection, he says, completely fail to understand God. You therefore deny not only reward but divine power, and should be deeply ashamed. I say it to your shame that such people can be found among you.
